attempts.prompt:
Use case: text-localization.
Asset type: transparent Chinese mobile puzzle game title sprite, final delivery canvas 720 × 180.
Input image 1: the exact typography and rendering reference, current title “泡泡来袭！”. Edit this wordmark into a matching sibling in the VERY SAME lettering family. Keep the round plump hand-drawn Chinese letter shapes, inflated smooth candy-like 3D faces, soft rounded stroke endings, thick rounded outer outline, short downward extruded outline depth, upper-left specular highlights and inner soft shading from this reference. Treat the supplied reference as the strict style master, not loose inspiration.
Text (verbatim): “困难关卡”.
EXACTLY FOUR simplified Chinese characters, left to right: 困 / 难 / 关 / 卡. 困 is an enclosed 木 within 囗; 难 has 又 and 隹; 关 and 卡 must be fully legible. No punctuation and no exclamation mark. No extra text.
Change only the wording and color family. Front letter faces: bright yellow #FFD25A at the top, smoothly vertically grading through vivid orange to orange-red #FF5A2E at the bottom. Deep wine-red #6E1414 thick continuous outer outlines, a darker red lower extrusion. Preserve the reference's relative outline thickness, rounded depth and shiny highlights. High-quality soft sculpted lettering, not an angular system font, not flat vector type.
Four plump glyphs form one centered horizontal line with slight natural lively variation as in the reference; almost fill the wide canvas while keeping every outline and bottom depth fully inside. Match reference text height and visual weight. Clean readable character counters; generously round terminals; width-to-height of complete wordmark about 4.1:1.
Genuinely transparent RGBA background, no white matte, no opaque background. Keep all background and holes transparent. Only the four-character wordmark. No arrows, backdrop glow, sparks, lightning, stars, bubbles, decorations, badge, banner, floating particles, cast shadow detached from lettering, watermark or logo.
attempts.superseded_reason: Narrow left radical in the second character was ambiguous; corrected with clear crossed strokes in v02.

attempts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / text-localization.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the transparent finished wordmark “困难关卡”.
Input image 2 is a supporting type-family reference only: the game's original “泡泡来袭！” wordmark.
ONE precise correction only. In the SECOND character 难, correct and clarify its LEFT component 又. The current left radical is too narrow and bulbous and OCR misreads it as the three-dot water radical 氵, giving 淮. It MUST unambiguously be 难, NOT 淮.
Draw the left 又 as exactly TWO clear intersecting thick round strokes: (1) a DISTINCT nearly horizontal top bar leading into a long diagonal stroke descending down-left (横撇), (2) a second continuous diagonal sweeping from upper-left to lower-right (捺), with a clear central crossing. Its lower half must visibly read as an X / crossed fork, not three staggered droplets. Give that top horizontal bar enough width and retain an obvious triangular negative space between the top bar and the crossing. Both strokes stay plump and rounded, but their intersecting structure is unmistakable. Keep this 又 sufficiently wide for legibility at a final 720×180 image size. Preserve the right component 隹 of 难.
Text remains EXACTLY “困难关卡”, four simplified Chinese characters, no punctuation. Do not replace 难 with traditional 難. No other wording changes.
KEEP EVERYTHING ELSE from image 1 as exactly unchanged as possible: all three other glyphs, rounded candy-like type family, letter height and width, layout, baseline, original color gradient, dark thick outline, short solid downward extruded depth, sculpted highlights, edge lighting, spacing, transparent background. No extra objects or effects. Do not add arrows, stars, sparkles, glow, exclamation mark or watermark. Genuinely transparent RGBA with clean edges.
This is NOT a full redesign. Repair the ambiguous 又 in 难 only; preserve the rest of the artwork.
attempts.correction: Clarified the top horizontal stroke and central crossing of the left radical in the second character while preserving the lettering style.
